title: deep-quant-standup-sprint-capture-nov04-2026
body:
Weekly capture from the Applied ML standup (deep quant track) — raw notes and experiment log. Intentionally informal: rough numbers, hypotheses, and triage items.

Summary:
- Focus this week: 1) get 4-bit per-layer mixed quant runs stable on v1.8 of the small-llama-family, 2) validate eval harness for instruction-following prompts, 3) reduce cold-start KV-cache overhead in onboarding path.
- Outcome: two reproducible runs (fp16 baseline + 4bit-gemmlowp variant) with comparable token-level perplexity within 3%, but 2.6x reduction in GPU memory at batch=8. Still seeing ~12ms added latency for cache warmup on first request path.

Attendees:
- Aisha (notes), Benji, Sophie, Diego, Lina, Rahul (infra), Maya (SRE async)

Agenda items + notes:
1) Quantization sanity runs
- Baseline: small-llama-7b fp16 (seq=2048)
  - mean generation latency (1000 tokens): 135 ms/token at batch=1 (test host: p4d.24xlarge-like sim)
  - memory peak: 19.8 GB
- Candidate: mixed-4bit-per-layer (round-to-nearest + group-size=128)
  - latency: 142 ms/token (+5.2%)
  - memory peak: 7.6 GB (-61.7%)
  - eval delta (instruction set A, 1k examples): 2.8% increase in perplexity vs baseline, but human pass@1 unchanged on small subset (n=200 manual checks)
- Observations: quant artifacts are concentrated on mathematical tokens and long-tail factual recall. Hypothesis: group-size 128 is too coarse for small dense layers. Next experiment: mixed group sizes (64 for first 8 layers, 128 rest).

2) Eval harness results and flaky metrics
- Issue: our current batching harness occasionally shuffles seed order, causing +-1.5% variance on pass@k metrics between runs. Added deterministic seed seeding at process start (PR linked above).
- Edge-case prompts: model hallucinations spike on two prompt templates that contain inline markdown tables. Created a minimal repro and filed JIRA JIRA-MLINF-2213.

3) Onboarding / KV-cache warmup
- Problem: private deployment onboarding path pulls KV-cache from object-store and applies a tokenized prefix rehash that costs ~12ms extra on first call (p50). Subsequent calls hit warm cache and drop to expected latency.
- Quick wins: prefetch top-1k prefixes during deployment rollout; optional background daemon to populate hot entries for the first 10 minutes. Infrastructure concerns about memory pressure on constrained Private installs.
- Action: Rahul to prototype prefetch daemon; Lina to run cost model for memory vs latency trade.

4) Canary & rollout concerns
- Canary observed one tail OOM during 4-bit run with batch=16 & seq=4096. Root cause likely incorrect KV-cache eviction policy under quant mem layout. Diego to reproduce with instrumentation + small heap dumper.

Experiment log (detailed runs):
- run_20261103_q4_mix_01: model small-llama-7b, quant=mixed-4bit, group=128, batch=8, seq=2048
  - gpu_mem_peak=7.6GB, avg_latency_token=142ms, eval_perplexity=18.7, notes=stable for 10 iterations, small increase in math errors
- run_20261103_q4_group64_first8: group sizes [64 first8, 128 rest], batch=8, seq=2048
  - gpu_mem_peak=8.4GB, avg_latency_token=144ms, eval_perplexity=18.2, notes=perplexity closer to fp16 baseline
- run_20261104_fp16_baseline: fp16, batch=8, seq=2048
  - gpu_mem_peak=19.8GB, avg_latency_token=135ms, eval_perplexity=17.7

Failed runs and triage:
- run_20261102_q4_badscale: encountered nan in softmax during forward when layernorm epsilon was 1e-5. Quick patch: increase epsilon to 1e-4 in quant path. Re-ran and stable. Ticket created: MLINF-2220.
- run_20261103_kv_warmup_spike: onboarding job spikes when object-store latency > 80ms. Need SLO for object-store latency; currently missing. Maya (SRE) to add monitoring alert.

Code/infra notes:
- PR to serving-runtime to add deterministic seeding and improved eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5421 (review in progress).
- Small helper script added: tools/quant/eval_miniprofile.sh — runs the minimal eval suite and returns a small CSV of token-latency percentiles.

Decisions / proposals made in meeting:
- Accept mixed-4bit as an experimental default for small-llama family for Dedicated tier; require continuous eval gating (perplexity + a small human-verified QA sample) before canary.
- For Private onboarding, make KV-prefetch optional toggle with safe memory ceiling parameter; default OFF for air-gapped installs.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Diego: reproduce canary OOM with heap dumper + instrumented trace. Due 2026-11-06.
- Rahul: prototype KV prefetch daemon and run memory/time trade experiment on a t4g-like node. Due 2026-11-10.
- Lina: cost model doc (3 scenarios: hosted, dedicated, private constrained) for prefetch vs latency. Due 2026-11-09.
- Benji: add deterministic seeding to the distributed eval harness tests and extend unit tests for batch order. PR feedback by 2026-11-07.
- Aisha: prepare canary checklist for mixed-4bit rollout (include eval harness snapshot + manual QA prompts). Due 2026-11-08.

Open questions for next week:
- How aggressive can group-size mixing be for larger models (13b+) without manual tuning? Start small and collect metrics.
- Should we add a tiny synthetic workload to onboarding that primes the KV-cache by simulating expected prefix distributions? Concern: synthetic priming may bias initial metric collection.

References and quick links:
- Eval instructions: confluence://CONF-897-quant-strategy (see section "onboarding evals")
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5421
- Jira: JIRA-MLINF-2213 (prompt hallucination repro), MLINF-2220 (layernorm epsilon fix)

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Try a hybrid 3-bit/4-bit layer for the last two MLP layers (it might reduce perplexity for arithmetic tokens).
- Consider early-exit for KV-prefetch: only prefetch top-k prefixes observed in last 24h for that customer. Good for Dedicated customers with steady workload.
- Save a small reproducible seedset (n=128) for manual QA that includes markdown tables, math, and factual recall. Store under /datasets/evals/manual-qa-128 for future onboarding checks.

Meeting closed — next sync Tues 2026-11-10 10:30 PT.
